newsitem.title: USA: Estrogen may help women with Alzheimer's.
newsitem.headline: Estrogen may help women with Alzheimer's.

text.p: Oestrogen therapy may help women with Alzheimer's disease recover memory and concentration, according to a small research project presented at a neuroscience conference on Wednesday.

The study lasted only 13 weeks and involved only a half-dozen women, but it is the second tantalizing recent report on possible links between the female hormone and the debilitating neurological disease.

Geriatrician Dr. Sanjay Asthana said he got the idea for the experiment after seeing a recent report that women who take oestrogen replacement therapy for at least 10 years after menopause reduce the risk of Alzheimer's by 30 to 40 percent.
"That really struck me," he said. "If that were true, might oestrogen also improve some of the symptoms of Alzheimer's disease?"
Asthana, who carried out the experiment with colleagues at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and the University of Washington, presented the study at the Society of Neuroscience meeting here.

He found that eight weeks of oestrogen therapy through a patch significantly helped the six women, who were followed for an additional five weeks after the treatment ended. Neurological tests showed their ability to pay attention and their memory improved while they took the hormone but the benefits diminished when they stopped, he said.
"The findings are promising," he said. "This work forms the basis for further research."
